# `silk/mem/prefetch`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Cache prefetch hints: tell the processor that the program will soon use the memory at a pointer.

## When to use
Use [`Prefetch.hint`](#Prefetch.impl.hint) or [`Prefetch.hintMany`](#Prefetch.impl.hintMany) in a hot loop that reads memory in an order the
processor cannot predict, such as the next node of a linked structure or a table entry chosen
by a hash, when a measurement shows that the loop waits for memory. Issue the hint a few
iterations before the access, so that the memory is in cache when the access comes.

## Details
A hint is only a request. It never reads or writes memory, never faults, and never changes what
the program computes, so it is safe with any pointer, also null or released memory. The
[`PrefetchOptions`](#PrefetchOptions) argument is static and selects the access (read or write), the locality
(how long to keep the memory in cache) and the cache (data or instruction).

On x86_64 and AArch64 a hint is one prefetch instruction, such as `prefetcht0` or
`prfm pldl1keep` for a read with high locality. A target without a prefetch instruction, such as
WebAssembly, ignores the hint.

## Gotchas
A hint that comes too late, or that requests memory the program does not use, costs time and
cache space. Measure before and after you add one.

## Examples
### Prefetch the next element while you sum an array
```silk
import silk.mem.pointer { Pointer }
import silk.mem.prefetch { Prefetch, PrefetchAccess, PrefetchCache, PrefetchLocality, PrefetchOptions }

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  let values = [3, 5, 8, 13, 21]
  let mut sum = 0
  let mut at: usize = 0
  while at < values.length {
    if at + 1 < values.length {
      Prefetch.hint<i32>(Pointer.fromRef<i32>(&values[at + 1]), PrefetchOptions {
        access: PrefetchAccess.Read,
        locality: PrefetchLocality.High,
        cache: PrefetchCache.Data,
      })
    }
    sum = sum + values[at]
    at = at + 1
  }
  if sum != 50 {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```

Import as `Prefetch` with `import silk.mem.prefetch { Prefetch }`.

<a id="PrefetchLocality"></a>

## `PrefetchLocality`

```silk
pub enum PrefetchLocality
```

How long a prefetched cache line is likely to stay useful.

### Details

The levels are `0` to `3` of the `llvm.prefetch` locality. On x86_64, a read hint with
`NoReuse` is `prefetchnta`, `Low` is `prefetcht2`, `Moderate` is `prefetcht1` and `High` is
`prefetcht0`.

<a id="PrefetchLocality.NoReuse"></a>

### `NoReuse`

```silk
NoReuse
```

The program uses the memory one time. Keep it out of the caches as much as possible.

<a id="PrefetchLocality.Low"></a>

### `Low`

```silk
Low
```

The program uses the memory again soon, a little.

<a id="PrefetchLocality.Moderate"></a>

### `Moderate`

```silk
Moderate
```

The program uses the memory again several times.

<a id="PrefetchLocality.High"></a>

### `High`

```silk
High
```

The program uses the memory again many times. Keep it in every cache level.

## `PrefetchOptions`

```silk
pub struct PrefetchOptions
```

The static selections of one prefetch hint.

### Details

A read of data with `High` locality is the common hint. It is `prefetcht0` on x86_64 and
`prfm pldl1keep` on AArch64. Hints for the instruction cache ignore `access`.

<a id="PrefetchOptions.access"></a>


Whether the program will read or write the memory.

<a id="Prefetch.impl.hint"></a>

### Associated function `hint`

```silk
pub fn hint<T>(pointer: ?*const T, static options: PrefetchOptions) -> ()
```

Hints that the program will soon use the memory at `pointer`, as `options` selects.

#### Details

It does not read or write memory and does not fault, also when `pointer` is null or addresses
released memory, and it never changes what the program computes. `options` is static, so the
hint is fixed at compile time. A target without a prefetch instruction, such as WebAssembly,
ignores it.

ignores it.
